questions.question: Network config in Git — primary win:
options: History, review, blame, and rollback of intent—not magic correctness by itself
Git pushes to devices automatically always

questions.question: Pull request for a fabric change should show:
options: Diff of intent, risk notes, test evidence, and rollback—not just 'LGTM' on a 5k-line dump

questions.question: CI for network automation should at least:
options: Lint/syntax-check, unit tests, and render/validate configs before merge
Deploy straight to prod on commit

questions.question: Continuous delivery to network devices differs from app CD because:
options: Blast radius, change windows, and partial failure modes dominate—canaries and health gates are mandatory

questions.question: YAML in network IaC — top footgun:
options: Indentation/structure errors and ambiguous types (on/off, numbers)—validate schema, don't trust eyes

questions.question: JSON vs YAML for machine APIs:
options: JSON is ubiquitous for APIs; YAML is common for humans/config—both need schemas and validation

questions.question: Sensible pipeline stages:
options: lint → unit → lab/cOS → canary → prod with holds
skip lab if CI green on lint only

questions.question: Long-lived config branches diverge because:
options: Reality and trunk move on—prefer short-lived branches and frequent rebase/merge

questions.question: Immutable artifacts in NetDevOps mean:
options: Build once (image/package/rendered bundle), promote the same artifact through environments
Edit prod by hand after deploy

questions.question: Policy-as-code for network changes:
options: Encode constraints (prefix limits, banned patterns) checked in CI—not only human review

questions.question: Config drift detection belongs in NetDevOps because:
options: Live state diverges from Git—detect, alert, and reconcile deliberately

questions.question: Can you commit encrypted secrets?
options: Sometimes with sealed/vault patterns—but prefer external secret stores; never plain secrets

questions.question: Who should review a routing policy PR?
options: Someone with domain competence and blast-radius accountability—not only 'any approver'

questions.question: Rollback strategy should be:
options: Tested, owned, and fast—prefer forward-fix only when truly safer and rehearsed

questions.question: Feature flags / safe toggles for network features:
options: Allow dark launch and quick disable when software supports it—pair with metrics

questions.question: CODEOWNERS-style ownership helps:
options: Route reviews to teams accountable for that domain (edge vs fabric vs tools)

questions.question: Why track dependency versions for network tooling?
options: Supply-chain and break-glass rebuilds—pin and patch deliberately
Latest always safest with no testing

questions.question: Lab that doesn't mirror prod topologies fails because:
options: False confidence—invest in representative labs or risk production-only learning
Prod is the only ethical testbed

questions.question: ChatOps for network changes—guardrail:
options: Authenticate, authorize, audit, and rate-limit—chat is a UI, not a security boundary
Anyone in Slack may push prod

questions.question: Pipeline success metric that can mislead:
options: Deploy frequency without change failure rate / MTTR—optimize the whole DORA-like set carefully for networks
